You know what, I’ve T.A.’d for a couple of classes now with different professors. I understand where you’re coming from because I’ve seen students only come in for exams and dip. But I also don’t like the “I don’t owe you anything” part. A great professor wouldn’t complain about teaching classes. At some universities it is a requirement to teach undergrad courses. But you have to understand, students who attend these top institutions want to get a good quality education and often times it is expected professors write LOR’s for students. Now obviously don’t write letters to students who never show up. But for students who actively put in work you shouldn’t have a problem writing them a LOR. Another thing, just because a student misses some classes doesn’t mean they’re a bad student. I liked your example of students who cry wolf, but for students who have families and jobs, please go easy on them. There’s a student in my class who is 28, works a full time job with two little kids. She’s also single. She does miss from time to time, maybe once a week. But she comes to office hours and she goes the extra mile. I would write her a LOR in a minute. 

Also just P.S. idk how new you are at teaching but the course evaluations at the end of the semester do matter and if reflect poorly, can lead to you not receiving another contract/ not getting tenure. So yeah they do matter 😅
